mahunag.place: Bakhari Kothi (Mahunag), about 25 km from Karsog
mahunag.about: The best-known temple of the Karsog valley, dedicated to Mahunag, who is worshipped here as Karna, the generous warrior of the Mahabharata. People from all over Mandi district come here to pray, and the temple hosts the valley’s biggest fair every May.
mahunag.story: Locals believe that after the Mahabharata war, Karna’s last rites were performed near Tattapani on the Sutlej, and that the devta later appeared here as Mahunag.
when: Mid-May, during the Mahunag Mela, for the fair, music and crowds
Any time from spring to autumn for a quieter visit
tips: Dress modestly and take off your shoes before entering the temple area
Combine it with Mamleshwar Mahadev and Kamaksha Devi for a one-day temple circuit
fairs: mid-May (about 14–19 May), a five-day fair with folk music and dance

mamleshwar.place: Mamel village, about 1 km from Karsog bus stand
mamleshwar.about: An ancient Shiva temple built in the traditional wood-and-stone style, right next to Karsog town. It is known for the unusual old objects kept inside, and it leads Karsog’s main spring fair.
mamleshwar.story: Tradition says the Pandavas stayed here during their exile. Inside you can see a large drum said to be Bhima’s, a sacred fire that locals say has been burning since that time, and a huge old grain of wheat believed to date from the Pandavas.
when: Mahashivratri (February–March) and Shravan Mondays (July–August) for special worship
April, when the Nalwar Mela opens with the temple’s procession
tips: Easy to walk to from Karsog town
Photography rules inside the temple can vary; ask before taking pictures
fairs: 5–11 April in most years (not held every year)

kamaksha.place: Kao village, about 7 km from Karsog
kamaksha.about: One of the main goddess temples of the valley, dedicated to Durga as Maa Kamaksha. The carved wooden temple in a quiet village setting is a lovely short trip from Karsog town.
kamaksha.story: Locals believe the sage Parashurama installed the goddess here, and that she was once the family goddess of the old Suket kingdom.
when: Navratri (March–April and September–October), the busiest and most festive time
Any clear day for a quieter visit
tips: Pair it with Mamleshwar Mahadev and Mahunag for a temple day
Carry cash for small offerings; there are no ATMs in the village
fairs: twice a year, March–April and September–October

shikari_devi.place: Shikari peak, about 3,359 m, above Janjehli
shikari_devi.about: A goddess temple on the highest peak of Mandi district, with sweeping Himalayan views and forest all around. It is famous for having no roof.
shikari_devi.story: Locals believe the Pandavas worshipped the goddess here during their exile, and that every attempt to build a roof over the shrine has failed. Many also say snow never settles on the idol.
when: April to June and September to November
The road usually closes in winter because of snow
tips: It is cold at the top even in summer; carry a warm layer and rain protection
Check the weather and road before you go
fairs: March–April and September–October, when the road is open

kamrunag.place: High in the forest above Rohanda, about 3,334 m
kamrunag.about: A temple beside a small sacred lake deep in deodar forest, reached on foot. Kamru Nag is worshipped across Mandi district as the god of rain.
kamrunag.story: Locals identify Kamru Nag with Barbarik, a warrior of the Mahabharata. Devotees offer coins and jewellery into the lake as a sign of faith.
when: Late spring to autumn, when the trail is open
Mid-June for the big annual fair at the lake
tips: Wear good walking shoes; the last part is a forest trek
Offerings in the lake are sacred; don’t touch or remove anything

chindi.place: Chindi village, about 14 km from Karsog on the Shimla road
chindi.about: A beautifully carved goddess temple among apple orchards and deodar trees at Chindi, a popular stop on the Karsog–Shimla road with an HPTDC hotel nearby.
chindi.story: Locals say the goddess showed a priest the plan of the temple through a line of ants, and that the name Chindi comes from “chinti”, the word for ant.
when: 2–4 August for the Chindi Mata Mela
Spring and autumn for orchard views and clear skies
tips: Easy to combine with a drive to Tattapani or Shimla

pangna.about: An old goddess temple on the top floor of the historic Pangna Fort tower, still in daily worship. The fort is one of the oldest buildings of the area, built in the traditional Kath-Kuni style of timber and stone that stands up well to earthquakes.
pangna.story: Pangna was an early seat of the Suket rulers, and the temple and fort tower are among the area’s most important heritage sites.
when: Any time of year; early June for the local Katal Mela
tips: See the fort tower and old houses of Pangna village
Combine with a drive via Churag

chawasi.place: Mahog, in the Chawasi area of Karsog
chawasi.about: The temple of Nag Chawasi Siddh, the main devta of the Chawasi area, in a village setting in the hills of Karsog.
chawasi.story: Locals believe the old Suket kings honoured the devta with gifts that are still kept at the temple.
when: 12–15 May for the Chawasi Utsav at Nahvindhar
About a month after Diwali for Budhi Diwali at Mahog
tips: Ask locally about road conditions before driving up

dhamuni.about: The temple of Nag Dhamuni, one of the most important devtas of the Karsog valley, at Seri Bungalow.
dhamuni.story: Locals believe Nag Dhamuni came to the Karsog side from the Kullu hills and made this area his home.
when: The Seri Bhanju Mela in late August or September
tips: See the drone photos of Seri Bungalow on this site before you go
fairs: starts on Rishi Panchami (late August or September), three days

laxmi_narayan.about: A temple in the heart of Karsog’s old bazaar, with an evening aarti every day. It is easy to visit while walking around town.
when: Janmashtami (August–September), when the old bazaar celebrates
tips: Visit at aarti time in the evening
